title: Evaluate: should Sunrise Bakery open a second shop?
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 48 (Pupil PDF worksheet: own exam-style questions, case data and mark-scheme points (teacher-written))
intro: Lesson 48. Use the case data. Plan in the frame, then write in the portal response box. All businesses, people and figures in these cases are fictional, made up for practice.

passage.title: Sunrise Bakery: a second shop
paras: Sunrise Bakery is a sole trader business owned by Maryam in Leicester. She employs 4 staff and sells bread and cakes from one shop. Each week she sells 1,200 loaves at £2.50 each. Her weekly total costs are £2,100. Rent is £400 a week. A supermarket with an in-store bakery is opening nearby next month. Maryam is choosing between hiring a delivery driver (£420 a week) and using a delivery app that takes 25% of each order.

A second shop in a nearby town would cost £45,000 to fit out. Maryam expects it to bring in revenue of £120,000 a year. She has £20,000 of savings and a family friend has offered to be a partner in a musharakah (sharing profit and loss). Her current profit is about £46,800 a year (£900 a week).

questions.q: Evaluate whether Sunrise Bakery should open a second shop.
questions.a: Level-marked (12): growth and revenue £120,000, economies of scale in buying; vs £45,000 cost (more than double her savings), sharing control and profit with a partner, the new supermarket threat, management stretched over two sites; judgement with 'it depends on'.

frame.label: For: point and chain of reasoning in context
Against: point and chain of reasoning in context
Judgement: decide, give the main reason, say what it depends on

markScheme.a: Level 4 (10-12): developed chains on both sides in context and a supported judgement with 'it depends on'. Level 3 (7-9): both sides developed, judgement partly supported. Level 2 (4-6): some development, one-sided or generic. Level 1 (1-3): points identified.
